reviews.review:
It's an odd game.

ARPGs are about having a build idea, moving forward with it by focusing on paths and avenues the game has to progress it, and to take it to ends of the game.

This game is about taking what drops you have, altering completely what you do based on those drops, and getting lucky enough to get carried forward. There is no builds here; attribute points do so little in terms of lowering and mitigating damage as to be almost useless. The only progression found in game is to either die or win a round and take what meta-progression you acquire to boost your account for when you start the game. 

Items are dropped based on level, which scales somewhat to what attributes they can boost, but more importantly, the base damage of an item. The only good path I see so far in game is to get lucky enough to drop a high damage item that can carry you for a few levels. This is much harder at level 1, where you are introduced to game, as zones to adjust to your level as you level. Instead creatures are the level where you started the zone at. I was level 7 when I ended the first zone, where it rescaled to level 7 enemies.

In that time of playing the first area, I ran into a few issues. There is no regeneration for health, which is what the entire difficulty of the game seems centered around. The only difficulty is how well you back up and dodge some attacks. Since enemies will stop where they are to attack you when in range, you backing up at a good speed will negate MOST things hitting you. Except range attacks.

Range attacks will auto target you up till the point the projectile is released. If the enemy has naturally fast projectile speed for its animation and enemy sprite, such as the goatmen in the desert area, they are the most dangerous creatures in game. The stones also have a solid chance of stunning you for two full seconds.

The second area, in contrast, was not as tough as I dropped a two handed weapon that took me from doing 70-90 damage per default to about 300-350 damage per auto attack. The weapon also had a small AoE lightning spell that was low cooldown, stuns all enemies for 2 seconds, and did base damage equal to the weapon for almost no mana cost. The only thing was semi-difficult afterward was the boss.

The boss will stand still and throw super fast poison canisters filled with spiders. If you damage him enough, it will cause him to be stunned for like five seconds. If you can time your dodges well enough, have enough damage, the round is over and you technically win, letting you exit that game, keeping your character and gear. 

What happens if you are in the middle of a run a need to do other things? Well too bad, you can leave your run and lose all your gear. That's your problem. It was at this point, I ALT+F4ed and probably will not be back without massive changes to how the game functions

In conclusion, the only benefit to playing this game is to semi-mindlessly backup, ogle over a lucky drop that defines or ruins your run by not dropping, dying ignobly, and either going back for more or quitting entirely.

Things to fix:
-Have some amount of progression in game for certain playstyles. You can play as a trapper but I saw no trapper abilities whatsoever
-Make your attributes actually affect your stats beyond a few HP per point with no scaling, compared to enemy health bars
-Either scale creatures to the level of the character as they progress through the zone or give some level scaling to loot as your progress through the zone.
-Give players some reason to continue playing the game. Two maps, no way to save and quit between runs, and no other incentives beyond some basic meta-progression.
reviews.developer_response:
Hello Akward!

Thank you for this incredibly detailed and analytical review. As a small 3-person team, we truly value feedback that dives this deep into the game's balance and mechanics. You’ve pointed out several core areas that we are actively looking at for our 2026 roadmap.

To address your specific points:

- Build Diversity vs. Loot Luck: We hear you. Currently, the game relies heavily on 'lucky drops' (like the lightning weapon you found). We are working on making attribute points and skill paths more impactful so that your build choices matter as much as the loot you find.

- Health Regeneration & Difficulty: The lack of passive regen is a deliberate hardcore choice, but we understand it can lead to tedious 'hit-and-run' gameplay. We are evaluating ways to introduce more tactical recovery options.

- Saving during a Run: This is a major point of friction. At least, we have implemented a pause function for singleplayer-mode.

- Scaling & Content: We are working on better dynamic scaling and, of course, more maps and playstyles (like the 'trapper' idea you mentioned) to give the game more depth. In fact, several new skills are planned for the next patch, including a trapper skill that will be available depending on the corresponding loot.

It’s clear you’ve put a lot of thought into how the game functions. We hope you’ll keep an eye on our updates throughout 2026. We are committed to turning this 'mess' into the polished experience we all want it to be.
Constructive criticism like yours is essential for our progress, even if the current recommendation is negative ;)

Best regards,
The Nightshift Game Development Team
